Q1: Tetraethylene glycol presents known significant inhalation hazards (Tier 1) based on GHS classifications, and potential hazards for dermal/eye exposure and carcinogenicity/mutagenicity/reproductive effects (Tier 2). It is considered to have a favorable safety profile for environmental and oral hazards (Tier 3), but data is deficient for endocrine disruption and organ/systemic hazards (Tier 4).
Q2: Tetraethylene glycol is not identified on any lists of concern. It appears on the SCIL Half Green Circle list, indicating it is generally considered of low concern based on available experimental and modeled data, though further data would strengthen this conclusion.
Q3: This chemical is well-characterized in the scientific literature, with over 9,400 references, and has a defined molecular structure. While it has some toxicological study evidenced by 11 records in the ToxValDB, it has not undergone comprehensive EPA evaluations (IRIS or PPRTV) and exhibits data deficiencies for endocrine disruption and organ/systemic hazards.
